selection_reason: The frozen full-grid development result shows 2+1 retains substantially lower accepted-logical error than 3+1 while using one fewer round. The next direct resource question is whether the terminal verification round in 2+1 is necessary for accepted-logical safety.

protocol.round_block: identical 39-two-qubit-gate firewall round used by the frozen benchmark
protocol.syndrome_estimator: two complete unflagged center frames must agree bit-for-bit; disagreement => HOLD
protocol.pre_recovery_fail_closed: any center flag or detected ancilla loss => HOLD; detected data loss => QUARANTINE
protocol.recovery: map agreed firewall-basis frame b to frozen center frame s and apply the frozen decoder as a classical Pauli-frame update
protocol.acceptance: if both acquisition records are complete, unflagged, loss-free and equal, ACCEPT immediately after recovery; no terminal verification round
protocol.accepted_output_scoring: protected logical quotient after analysis-only ideal cleanup; dressed residual weight reported separately

fault_semantics: identical p/q/p_loss definitions and conditional Pauli distributions to the frozen parent benchmark

evaluation_plan.higher_order_grid: same exact <=2 plus frozen conditional N>=3 tail-Monte-Carlo method, 200000 tail shots per nonzero grid point
evaluation_plan.master_seed: same master with distinct protocol id 4

stop_rules: This candidate cannot retroactively alter the frozen 1+0/2+1/3+1 benchmark.
If 2+0 has a first-order accepted-logical term, record it; do not add verification after exposure within this version.
Any follow-on adaptive rule is a new candidate.
